Subject: Post-call recap: TCO & token economics for Nimbus Health

Hi Laura / Ashok —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we all have the same view.

Goal / success criteria you shared:
- Reduce inference cost by ~60% vs current managed provider run-rate while preserving generation quality for patient-facing summaries.
- Maintain 95p latency < 250ms for critical read flows (peak: ~120 rps).
- Keep PHI in-region and integrate with your KMS for key management.

Top pain points from the call:
1) Token spend unpredictability — spikes during end-of-month reporting and care-bot campaigns.
2) High cost of synchronous single-request model inference at peak.
3) Concerns about latency at peak and cache warm-up.
4) Compliance / KMS requirements for PHI storage and audit logs.

Levers we discussed (high level):
- Model selection & size: route lower-risk flows to smaller, cheaper variants.
- Batching + continuous batching: reduces per-token compute at peak without impacting average latency for many flows.
- KV / prefix caching for repetitive prompts (e.g., templated discharge summaries).
- Quantized model variants for non-critical flows to lower GPU memory and cost.
- Smart routing: route best-effort or non-sensitive jobs to lower-cost regions (if policy allows).

Ballpark numbers & assumptions we used on call:
- Baseline: 1.2B tokens/month, 70% generation tokens, average prompt length 120 tokens.
- Target: reduce cost/unit by ~60% using batching + smaller model variants and caching (details in attached workbook).

Attachments: I attached a short TCO summary and the estimate workbook (nimbus_estimate_q3.xlsx, redwood_tco_summary.pdf).

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) Redwood: provide an updated TCO workbook and a 4-week pilot scope with measurable KPIs (cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency). Deliverable: updated workbook + pilot plan — Ben, by Wed 6/17.
2) Nimbus: share last 3 months token/usage export and any blacklisted prompts or PHI flags — Laura/Ashok, by Fri 6/19.
3) Schedule technical workshop (infrastructure + security) — propose Wed 6/24 or Thu 6/25; please confirm.

If this looks right I’ll get the updated workbook over and propose a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Ben

Laura — thanks, and totally understand the budget constraint. Attached is a short ROI sketch and the updated workbook (see files). Key assumptions I used for the example ROI:

- Baseline: 1.2M generated tokens/month (your estimate), current provider blended rate $0.060 per 1k tokens => baseline = $72k/month.
- Redwood pilot profile: route 45% of traffic to a 4B quantized variant and 55% to a 13B standard variant with batching and KV cache for 30% of requests.
- Batching + continuous batching: expected token-cost reduction = 28% at your weekday peak given 120-token prompts and 4-8 request aggregation window.
- KV / prefix caching: we modeled a 12% reduction in total generated tokens for templated summaries.
- Resulting blended rate estimate: ~$0.024 per 1k tokens -> estimated spend = $28.8k/month (~60% reduction).

Sample quick ROI (monthly):
- Current: $72,000/month
- Redwood (projected): $28,800/month
- Monthly savings: $43,200 -> payback on pilot infra/eng hours expected within 6–8 weeks if production adoption follows pilot.

Pilot scope (4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep): ingest usage export, set up isolated tenant with KMS and regional settings.
2) Week 1: baseline runs with 1:1 traffic mirror to Redwood (no reroute), initial metrics collection.
3) Week 2: enable batching + KV caching + quantized variant routing on non-critical flows.
4) Week 3: measure p95 latency, cost per 100k tokens, and run accuracy spot-checks vs baseline.

Deliverables: updated workbook (attached), pilot runbook, mutual action plan draft.

Links: cost calculator — https://app.redwood.com/cost-calculator/NIM-2026-042

If that looks OK I’ll lock the pilot dates. Proposed workshop: Wed 6/24 10:00–11:00 PT.
